summary: PhotoPrism is a self-hosted photo management system that uses machine learning models to automatically tag and organise image libraries. It allows you to browse, search, and share your personal collection through a web interface. The backend is written in Go and integrates with TensorFlow for image recognition.
goodFor: It suits individuals who want to organise large, self-hosted image collections with automated tagging without relying on external cloud services.
watchOut: Running TensorFlow inference locally can demand significant CPU or memory resources, and the AGPL-3.0 licence may impose constraints if you plan to modify and distribute the code.
deployNotes: You can typically run it using Docker with persistent volumes attached for your media library and configuration data. It generally requires a reverse proxy in front to handle HTTPS termination.
